subject: Post-call recap: ACME Analytics discovery — incident response & hyperscaler comparison
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@acme-analytics.com>, Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: ACME Analytics discovery — incident response & hyperscaler comparison

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from the discovery and the small set of asks we promised to follow up on: 

Summary from today
- Primary goal: reduce inference cost while improving p95/p99 latency predictability for interactive search and reranking.
- Main concerns you flagged: incident RCA timelines, notification windows, and whether fallbacks/transparent degradation exist compared to the hyperscaler you've used historically.
- Competitive context: you mentioned last month's hyperscaler outage that impacted batch scoring for ~3 hours and had an unclear RCA timeline.

What we (Redwood) will deliver by EOD Monday (attached):
- A compact SLA comparison matrix vs the major hyperscalers with objective dimensions (time-to-detect, time-to-notify, time-to-RCA, rollback/fallback behavior). See attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-sla-matrix.pdf
- A draft mutual action plan (MAP) that lists tests ACME wants us to run against a small test model and the timeline for each test. See attachment: MAP_ACME_Analytics_v1.docx
- An incident runbook excerpt showing our on-call escalation, notifications, and typical RCA cadence (initial triage within 15m, preliminary RCA within 24h, full RCA within 72h for production incidents). See attachment: incident_runbook_excerpt.txt

Proposed next tests (from today) — please confirm priorities:
1) Controlled failure (inject 20% dropped requests to replicate transient infra failure) — measure p50/p95/p99 and error propagation to clients.
2) Sustained spike (5x baseline qps for 15 minutes) to validate autoscaling / queueing behavior.
3) Cold vs warm KV cache pass to quantify cold-start amplification.
4) Fallback exercise: route to quantized-compatible variant on capacity pressure to validate quality delta and rollback time.

Questions for you
- Which of the above tests should be run first? (we recommend #2 then #4)
- Who on your Infra team should we coordinate with for test windows?

Next steps
- I’ll upload the mini-SLA matrix and MAP to the Drive and share the links (attached).
- Karthik will follow up with a proposed test harness and expected metrics.
- If these look good, can we lock a 2-hour test window the week of Aug 24?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-sla-matrix.pdf (pdf), MAP_ACME_Analytics_v1.docx (docx), incident_runbook_excerpt.txt (text)

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap and the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) The hyperscaler outage I referenced in July had a ~3 hour impact window, but we only received a preliminary blameless postmortem after 9 days and a final RCA after ~3 weeks. Our procurement/security team needs to see concrete timelines and a commitment on notification windows (pager/email) for Sev-2/Sev-1 incidents.

2) For the tests, we definitely want the sustained spike first (#2). For fallback (#4) we want to confirm whether quality regression is automatically surfaced to us (score deltas) and whether requests are dropped or degraded.

3) Our Infra folks are available on: infra@acme-analytics.com. Tom will coordinate a maintenance window for Aug 25 or Aug 26 (UTC morning).

4) Can you confirm whether Redwood retains audit logs for inference requests (API-level logs + token counts + request/response timestamps) for 90 days by default, and what the export process is? Also need to know what evidence you can provide for SOC2 and any encryption/KMS controls.

If you can include those items in the MAP and the SLA matrix that would be ideal.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Product, ACME Analytics
samira.k@acme-analytics.com | +1 (617) 555-2244

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: ACME Analytics discovery — incident response & hyperscaler comparison

Hi all —

Thanks Samira — quick technical answers and proposed acceptance criteria for each test. Quoted below where relevant.

(quote) "Can you confirm whether Redwood retains audit logs for inference requests... for 90 days" — short answer: yes, we provide request-level audit logs by default for 90 days on Hosted and Dedicated plans; Private deployments can configure retention via KMS/policy. We can provide an export as newline-delimited JSON or an s3-compatible export.

Test acceptance criteria (we recommend running in a sandbox account first):
- #2 Sustained spike (5x baseline for 15m): success if p95 latency increase <= 2.5x baseline, no more than 1% request errors, autoscaler transition < 90s; capture token-rate and GPU utilization.
- #4 Fallback exercise: success if fallback delivery time (time from start of overload to serving on fallback variant) < 45s and degradation in our internal quality metric < 6% measured on your held-out eval set. We will surface score deltas in a CSV after the test.
- #1 Controlled failure (20% dropped): success if client-facing error rate mirrors injected fault and time-to-notify (first alert to ACME) < 15m.
- #3 Cold vs warm cache: quantify delta in p99 and total tokens generated for both cases.

Incident / RCA timeline commitments (for Hosted & Dedicated):
- Detection: automated monitors + SRE paged in < 5m for Sev-1 in most cases.
- Notification: first contact within 15m (Slack ping + email) for Sev-1/Sev-2, incident channel created.
- Preliminary RCA: 24h target for context and triage notes.
- Final RCA: 72h target; if the root cause is dependent on hyperscaler/third party, we mark as dependent but provide mitigation and timeline updates every 12h.

We will add the above items to the MAP doc and include a short export of our audit log schema (fields: request_id, timestamp, model_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, status, latency_ms, client_id).

Operational notes
- For Private deployment customers we can map to your KMS/HSM and configure audit-export retention to match your policy.
- For Dedicated customers we offer an optional "incident warm standby" plan for faster manual intervention and prioritized capacity during major events (add-on).

I’ll attach a lightweight test harness script and the exact metrics we’ll produce.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
